Original Requirements: Build the Volopa OOP (Out-of-Pocket) Expenses API System using Laravel 10+ with PHP 8.2+. Three modules: 1. User Management & Permissions — RBAC via user_feature_permission with delegation hierarchy 2. Pocket Expense CSV Batch Upload — synchronous validation, async background sync 3. Single Expense Data Capturing — CRUD with FX conversion and flexible metadata
Product Goals: Enable comprehensive out-of-pocket expense tracking outside the Volopa card system
Implement secure role-based permission system with delegation capabilities
Provide efficient batch upload functionality for bulk expense data entry
Deliver automated FX conversion with user override capabilities
Ensure seamless integration with existing Volopa platform infrastructure
Maintain data integrity through comprehensive validation and error handling
Support flexible metadata capture for expense categorization and tracking
Provide atomic transaction processing for CSV batch operations
User Stories: As a Primary Admin, I want to enable OOP Expense feature for my client so that all users can start tracking out-of-pocket expenses
As a Primary Admin, I want to delegate expense management rights to other users so I can distribute workload
As an Admin, I want to manage expenses for users I've been granted access to so I can help with expense processing
As a Business User, I want to create individual expense records so I can track my out-of-pocket business expenses
As a Card User, I want the system to automatically convert foreign currency expenses so I don't have to calculate exchange rates
As an Admin, I want to upload CSV files with multiple expenses so I can efficiently enter bulk historical data
As a user, I want to see detailed validation errors when my CSV upload fails so I can correct the issues
As a Primary Admin, I want to revoke management rights from users so I can maintain proper access control
As a user, I want to configure custom expense sources so I can categorize expenses by payment method
As a user, I want to attach receipts and additional metadata to expenses so I can provide complete documentation
As an Admin, I want to be notified when batch uploads complete so I know when to review the processed expenses
As a user, I want to override automatically calculated FX conversion amounts so I can use actual transaction rates when available
Competitive Analysis: Expensify: Strong receipt scanning and automated categorization, but lacks multi-client delegation hierarchy
Concur SAP: Enterprise-grade approval workflows and FX conversion, but complex setup and limited CSV flexibility
Zoho Expense: Good batch import capabilities and custom fields, but weaker permission delegation model
Receipt Bank (Dext): Excellent document capture and integration, but limited multi-currency handling
Rydoo: Strong mobile experience and real-time FX rates, but lacks granular permission management
Chrome River: Robust approval workflows and audit trails, but poor batch upload user experience
Certify (Emburse): Good policy enforcement and reporting, but limited customization for expense sources

Requirement Analysis: The Volopa OOP Expenses system requires a sophisticated multi-layered architecture supporting three distinct but interconnected modules. The User Management module must implement a flexible RBAC system that goes beyond traditional role-based permissions to support delegation hierarchies where Primary Admins can grant specific management rights to any user regardless of their base role. The Pocket Expense CSV Batch Upload module needs synchronous validation with detailed error reporting and asynchronous background processing for approved batches, supporting up to 200 rows with atomic transaction guarantees. The Single Expense Data Capturing module requires real-time FX conversion with configurable sources, flexible metadata capture, and comprehensive validation. All modules must integrate seamlessly with existing Volopa platform infrastructure including OAuth2 authentication, multi-tenancy, and existing master data tables. The system must maintain strict data integrity through comprehensive validation, proper error handling, and audit logging while supporting both single-entry and bulk operations efficiently.
Requirement Pool: Implement user_feature_permission table and RBAC system with delegation hierarchy supporting Primary Admin, Admin, Business User, and Card User roles
Create pocket_expense table with comprehensive expense data capture including FX conversion, metadata, and file attachments
Build CSV batch upload system with synchronous validation, detailed error reporting, and asynchronous background processing for up to 200 rows
Implement automated FX conversion with 30-day lookback, client commission calculation, and user override capabilities
Create comprehensive API endpoints with proper authentication, authorization, validation, and error handling following Laravel best practices
Implement flexible expense source configuration with client-specific customization and soft delete support
Build notification system for batch upload completion and permission changes with configurable channels
UI Design draft: The system will be API-first with JSON responses designed for frontend consumption. Key API endpoints include: 1) Permission management endpoints for granting/revoking access with role-based authorization 2) Single expense CRUD endpoints with real-time FX conversion and metadata capture 3) CSV upload endpoints with file validation, error reporting, and progress tracking 4) Expense source configuration endpoints for client-specific customization. All endpoints follow RESTful conventions with proper HTTP status codes, consistent JSON response formats, and comprehensive error handling. The API supports pagination for list endpoints, filtering and sorting capabilities, and includes API Resources for consistent data shaping. Authentication uses OAuth2 middleware with proper client scoping and multi-tenancy support.
Anything UNCLEAR: Several project-level decisions remain unresolved: 1) The specific notification channel for batch upload completion (in-app, email, push, or combination) needs clarification 2) Whether FX conversion reuses existing platform FX service or requires new integration 3) The implementation approach for audit logging of permission grants/revokes 4) The exact query pattern for checking ClientFeatures model to determine if a client has OOP feature enabled. Additionally, some environment-level conventions need confirmation including soft delete pattern preference and table naming conventions (singular vs plural). These decisions should be made before implementation begins to ensure consistency with existing platform patterns.
